title: structured-output: unify constrained-decoding backends (CFG + regex) and tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: we maintain two constrained-decoding backends (CFG/grammar-based and regex-based) plus a tokenizer-aware matching layer. These implementations have diverged causing inconsistencies in structured-output enforcement (especially for nested CFGs, regex groups, and tokenizer boundary edgecases). This PR unifies the backends under a shared matcher API, improves tokenizer-aware regex handling (Unicode/emoji fallbacks), and adds a compatibility shim for the OpenAI-style function/tool-calling surface to ensure identical enforcement across streaming and non-streaming paths.

What this PR does: consolidates common parsing/matching code into runtime/structured/constraint_matcher.*, adds a unified CFG interpreter with deterministic expansion ordering, implements a tokenizer-aware regex engine that performs token-boundary-aware anchors and falls back to Unicode regex when tokenization splits characters, fixes several tokenizer edgecases (control chars, zero-width joiners, emoji sequences), and surfaces a stable error model to the OpenAI compatibility layer (so streaming token-by-token validation can gracefully fallback to post-emit validation when required).

Tests and verification: added a broad suite of unit and integration tests covering nested CFG rules, alternation precedence, greedy vs non-greedy regex in token-space, and explicit tokenizer boundary cases derived from our production corpus. Benchmarked performance impact on the streaming path and added a micro-batch cache for repeated rule checks to keep tokenization overhead sub-percent on typical prompts.

Migration notes: old backend adapters are preserved as thin shims for a release cycle; customers using custom CFG plugins should continue to work but are encouraged to validate their rule sets against the new stricter interpreter (see docs/structured-output/migration.md).

Related: closes ENG-2241, addresses SUP-4122 (customer-reported regex failure on emojis).

release_notes:
- Add unified constrained-decoding backends (CFG and regex) under runtime/structured.
- Tokenizer-aware regex engine with Unicode/emoji fallbacks to avoid false negatives on token boundaries.
- Streaming validator fallback semantics documented; improved stability for OpenAI-compat function/tool calling.
- Several tokenizer edgecase fixes (ZWJ, zero-width joiners, control characters).
- Migration guide added: docs/structured-output/migration.md
